calls.head: Who drives the play: the Sabres
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Sabres have been around the middle of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Sharks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Sabres’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.
calls.call: The Sabres get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.

calls.head: Bruisers vs. Finesse
calls.body: The Sharks hit a lot, but the Sabres mostly don’t. San Jose is one of the league’s best for physicality, and Buffalo is near the bottom. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Sharks.
calls.call: The Sharks hit more than the Sabres in the close stretches of the game.

BUF.head: We gave Buffalo a 64% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Colten Ellis stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Ellis stopped all 23 shots, worth 3.0 expected goals. That is more than Buffalo’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 60 starts.

story.head: Ellis shuts out the Sharks
paras: Olen Zellweger got the scoring started for the Sabres just 50 seconds into the second, and Zach Benson added the empty-netter with just under a minute left to make it 2-0.

The Sabres had the better of the chances, outshooting the Sharks 40-23. Colten Ellis turned aside all 23 shots for the Sabres, and Yaroslav Askarov made 38 saves in a losing effort. The Sabres improved to 5-4-3 and climbed off the bottom of the Atlantic to seventh, while the Sharks fell to 6-6-1, fourth in the Pacific.

items.text: The Sabres won for the first time in four games.
Zach Benson scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 15 (eleven games played since).
Both of the preview’s calls held.
